cause.published_convention_table: Token-index overlay via convention_tp_fp_fn: each whitespace token's slash-code tuple is assigned to at most one of 10 conventions. This is not a partition of the pooled bag counts.

mechanisms.description: Pooled micro F1 counts whole marked tokens via extract_morphemes (eat/en is one item; stem+codes must match). The published convention table uses whitespace token-index alignment and only the slash-code tuple. Those two units are not a partition of each other.

extract_morphemes matches sock/s inside sock/s}. or is/n't> . token_code_tuple does not strip } or >, so the convention overlay drops those marks. Extra marks inside {holds ... sock/s} action text are counted in the bag and often missed or undercounted in the index overlay. This is the residual on Sol/Gemini (0 failures, 0 unclassified gold).
On Luna, escape/ed vs escap/ed is bag FN+FP (different tokens) but convention-index TP because both have code ('ed',) at the same position.

Predicted sandwich/es, echo/es, child/ren, stone/z's are not in the 10 convention tuples. The bag still counts them as FP. They are rare and do not explain Sol/Gemini residuals (0 unclassified marks there).
Failed rows keep pooled TP=0 with bag FP/FN. The overlay still position-aligns a non-empty actual, so it can award convention TP on a failed speaker-mismatch row (Claude hard_02 Let/'us).
Ranking cells are ok with JSON ids aligned. Residual remains on aligned rows.

correction.going_forward: Keep pooled bag-of-morphemes as primary. Report per-convention figures by classifying each extracted mark into a convention (or UNCLASSIFIED) so convention TP/FP/FN partition the pooled totals.

cause.verdict: The difference is a reporting-script overlay, not gold-key error and not utterance-ID collapse. Pooled Stage 2 F1 is unchanged and remains primary.
